details:
I would like to propose a feature similar to VRChat's Shield Level system, but operating in the opposite direction.

Unlike Shield Level, which allows users to choose which avatars they want to load, this system would allow avatar owners to choose who is permitted to load their avatar.

Users who are not authorized should not receive the original avatar data. Instead, their client should display an Impostor or Fallback Avatar.

To make this feature practical, it could work similarly to the existing Interaction Permissions system. Players should be able to grant or revoke avatar loading permission for individual users through the Quick Menu at any time. This would allow creators to authorize only the people they are actually interacting with, while preventing automated accounts that simply join an instance to collect avatars.

This feature should be disabled by default. Players who are concerned about avatar security can choose to enable it, while everyone else can continue using VRChat exactly as they do today.

I believe this feature has become increasingly necessary due to the growing scale of avatar ripping. Recently, an avatar ripper within the Asian VRChat community used automated tools together with bot accounts to steal and resell more than 19,500 avatars. As AI-assisted tools continue to lower the technical barrier for avatar ripping, similar incidents are likely to become more common.

Current protection methods are no longer sufficient. Avatar obfuscation can increasingly be bypassed through AI-assisted analysis and other automated techniques, while avatar data can still be extracted after it has been loaded by the client. This incident also demonstrated that anti-cheat solutions such as Easy Anti-Cheat are not effective at preventing avatar ripping.

Currently, a bot account only needs to join an instance briefly to receive every visible avatar, even if it never interacts with anyone. With this feature, simply joining an instance would no longer be enough to collect avatars in bulk.

This proposal is intended to give players greater control over access to their own digital assets, while making large-scale automated avatar collection significantly more difficult.

Note: English is not my native language. If anything in this proposal is unclear or awkwardly worded, I appreciate your understanding and welcome any feedback.
title: Avatar Access Permission System
